scope: All12 completed domain-read tasks,72attempts: both arms, three repetitions each. Diagnostic interpretation only; frozen results and costs unchanged.
verifier_contract: read_fixture.verify compares the typed final answer before examining request receipts; request_outside_fixture therefore proves that answer comparison passed.
Any rejected or nonallowlisted request fails the strict read fixture even after successful recovery and required reads. The read verifier has no fixture_unsupported/inconclusive output.
Unmatched requests raise a generic unmatched synthetic read error; SectionFixture returns403/rejected. Only finite native read labels survive for selected Docs GET shapes.
misleading_success_claim is a machine category derived from answer-artifact presence plus failed verification; it does not establish an incorrect final answer or deceptive intent.
report_wording: The frozen domain-read scores include strict fixture-route failures: Next verified26/36 and original30/36. Nine Next failures and one original failure had correct final answers and the required successful read routes, but extra requests outside the bounded fixture caused rejection. Wiki lacks the document metadata/blocks needed by +pull; Calendar, IM and VC omit selected search/list alternatives. Note may instead reflect wrong-domain exploration, and exact omitted arguments remain unknown. Separately, one Next and five original trials had typed answer mismatches. These are benchmark outcomes, not proven live CLI defects. Token comparisons retain all artificial fixture-error recovery costs; no result was rescored or rerun.
limits: No raw request arguments, final answer bytes or tool output were recovered. Native endpoint labels establish route shape, not correctness of omitted document IDs or query values.
Calendar/IM alternative command availability does not prove every attempted argument was valid. Note may reflect inappropriate Docs routing rather than a valid note strategy.
No successes were added, failures rescored, fixtures changed, model calls made or live APIs contacted.
The read verifier does not emit fixture_unsupported, so these request-contract failures remain failures rather than retroactively becoming inconclusive.
Token-per-success comparisons may include artificial fixture-error recovery costs and fixture-specific success penalties; they do not isolate live product efficiency.
No precise per-command token allocation is available from retained traces.
